adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — Any authenticated user who is merely an attendee on any booking can push unlimited arbitrary addresses through this mutation, turning it into an unsolicited-email/ICS cannon sent from Cal's domain with the organizer's name in the From header.

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation explicitly authorizes any authenticated user who is an attendee on the booking (`isAttendee` check) to add arbitrary guest emails: `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;`. There is no limit on `guests` array length in `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (only `z.array(z.string().email())`), so an attendee can submit a large list of valid emails. The handler persists them (`attendees.createMany`) and then triggers outbound mail via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which sends an email (with an ICS attachment) to every attendee, and the attendee-facing template sets `from` to `${this.calEvent.organizer.name} <${this.getMailerOptions().from}>`, i.e., sent from Cal's domain while impersonating the organizer name. This makes the endpoint abusable as an unsolicited-email/ICS sender by any booking attendee.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is verifiable in the diff. Server-side input validation in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts` defines `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` (or other bound), so a direct TRPC call can submit an arbitrarily large list. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler will `createMany` attendee rows for the filtered `uniqueGuests` and then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which iterates over `calendarEvent.attendees` to send an email per attendee (plus organizer/team emails). There is also no server-side uniqueness constraint on the input array itself (the only uniqueness `refine` shown is client-side in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`), so duplicates can reach the handler and at minimum increase processing/email logic, and potentially create duplicate attendee rows depending on DB constraints. This enables a single request to trigger mass row creation and mass outbound email sends.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — The already-an-attendee filter uses case-sensitive === on raw strings, so the same address can be re-added indefinitely with different casing, defeating the uniqueGuests.length===0 gate and duplicating attendee rows and emails.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In addGuests.handler.ts the dedupe/existing-attendee filter compares `guest === attendee.email` without normalizing case, and the blacklist check lowercases the blacklist but compares it to the raw `guest`.
